title: Sign problem and criticality in world-line quantum Monte Carlo methods
abstract: Discussions of the sign problem usually focus on its role as the primary limitation of the applicability of quantum Monte Carlo methods for reliably solving quantum many-body models. Its behavior as a function of spatial lattice size, doping, temperature, and interaction strengths has been carefully characterized within the determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm. Here, we consider the much less well-explored question of the temperature- and size-dependence of the sign problem in the world-line quantum Monte Carlo method. We review how, in this algorithm, even sampling the partition function of free fermions yields a sign problem, which we connect to non-analytic behavior in the corresponding reference model, hard-core bosons on a lattice. The latter exhibits a finite-temperature Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition in 2D, and we show how this non-analytic behavior is imprinted on the average sign of the weights for the corresponding free fermion 2D tight-binding model. Our results thus show how phase-transition information can remain encoded in the sign problem even after direct sign sampling becomes impractical.
summary: This work tackles the sign problem in world-line QMC by showing that phase transition physics remains encoded in the average sign of the weights. By employing thermodynamic integration and finite-size scaling, the authors successfully locate the BKT transition in 2D and characterize crossovers in 1D, providing a powerful diagnostic tool for quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the temperature- and size-dependence of the sign problem in world-line Quantum Monte Carlo methods, specifically how phase-transition information can be extracted even when direct sampling fails.
main_result: The average sign ($\langle S angle_B$) successfully encodes phase transition information, allowing the location of the Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition in 2D and characterizing finite-size crossovers in 1D via thermodynamic integration techniques.
method: The authors employ world-line QMC updates and utilize thermodynamic integration (TI) to reconstruct free-energy differences ($\Delta f$) from the average sign, bypassing direct statistical limitations.
model_or_system: The study compares non-interacting spinless fermions to a reference hard-core-boson model on a lattice (1D ring and 2D square lattice). The Hamiltonian involves hopping terms ($t$) for both species.
key_observables: Average Sign ($\langle S angle_B$), Superfluid Density ($ho_s$), Free-Energy Density Difference ($\Delta f$), and the finite-size sign residual ($R(S)_L( eta)$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$) and lattice size ($L$), particularly near the critical temperature ($T_{BKT}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the free energy of the fermionic system remains analytic even if the average sign is not directly measurable, allowing the use of TI.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the superfluid density and average fermion sign vs. temperature, and show the finite-size sign residuals ($R(S)_L$) confirming the leading-logarithmic approach to a critical constant.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general principle of encoding phase transitions in the sign problem. It then details the 1D case using boundary condition ratios, followed by the 2D case where thermodynamic integration and finite-size scaling are used to locate the BKT transition.
why_interesting: The techniques developed for extracting critical information from the sign problem are highly relevant for studying quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated systems where direct simulation is impossible.
